Name: Mod Folder Cleaner - Find Duplicates and Clean Junk Files
Author: ZeroXPatch
Description:
Code at: https://github.com/ZeroXPatch/Projects-for-Nexus-Mod/blob/main/StardewModsCleaner.py

[b][size=5][center][color=#ffff00]Stardew Mods Cleaner[/color][/center][/size][/b]
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=downloads][center]https://www.nexusmods.com/profile/ZeroXPatch/mods?gameId=1303&sortBy=downloads[/center][/url]

Stardew Mods Cleaner is a small desktop utility that scans your Stardew Valley [b]Mods[/b] folder and helps clean up harmless clutter and common installation mistakes.

Nothing is deleted automatically. By default, all cleanup actions move files into a restoreable Trash folder.

This tool does not modify game files, save files, or mod content.

[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/40386/40386-1766207777-1210773015.png[/img]

[line][b][color=#00ff00]What this tool flags and why
[/color][/b]
OS metadata files (safe)These files often come from the creator’s operating system or ZIP extraction and are common in Nexus downloads.
Examples:
[list]
[*][code].DS_Store[/code]
[*][code]Thumbs.db[/code], [code]ehthumbs.db[/code]
[*][code]._*[/code] (macOS AppleDouble files)
[*][code]Icon[/code]
[*][code]__MACOSX[/code] folder
[/list]These files are not used by Stardew Valley or SMAPI.

[b]Default: auto-selected, safe to remove.[/b]
[line][b][color=#00ff00]Empty top-level folders (safe)
[/color][/b]
Empty folders directly inside the Mods folder, usually left behind after removing or updating mods.

[b]Default: auto-selected, safe to remove.[/b]
[line][b][color=#00ff00]Duplicate mods (same SMAPI UniqueID)
[/color][/b]
Detects multiple installed copies of the same mod using [code]manifest.json[/code] UniqueID, not folder name.
These can cause version conflicts or unexpected behavior.
[b]Not auto-selected. User review required.[/b]
[line][b][color=#00ff00]Nested “Mods/Mods” folders
[/color][/b]
Detects mods extracted one folder too deep, which can prevent them from loading correctly.
The tool can flatten these folders by moving valid mod folders into the correct location.
[b]Not auto-selected. User review required.[/b]
[line][b][color=#00ff00]Archive leftovers (optional)
[/color][/b]
ZIP/RAR/7Z files left in the Mods folder after extraction.
[b]Off by default. Optional cleanup.[/b]
[line][b][color=#00ff00]Safety notes

[/color][/b][list]
[*]All actions use a restoreable Trash folder by default
[*]Each item shows a “Why is this flagged?” explanation
[*]No mod logic or assets are modified
[/list]


[b][color=#ff0000][size=3]Advanced Version includes the following (Use with Caution) : 
[/size][/color][/b]
[b][color=#ffff00]CAUTION: Include desktop.ini
[/color][/b]
[b]What it is:[/b] [code]desktop.ini[/code] is a Windows Explorer metadata file that stores folder display settings (folder icon, view mode, localized name, etc.).

[b]Why it’s flagged:[/b] It’s not used by Stardew Valley or SMAPI. It’s “system noise” that sometimes appears inside mod folders.

[b]Is it safe to remove?
[/b]
Usually yes for the game, but:
[list]
[*]It can remove custom folder view/icon settings in Windows Explorer.
[*]Windows may recreate it later.
[*]Some mod authors might include it for cosmetic folder presentation.
[/list][b]Why it’s caution:[/b] It’s harmless for gameplay, but affects Windows folder appearance and can confuse people when it reappears.
[line][b][color=#ffff00]CAUTION: Log clutter inside mod folders (log.txt, *.log, *.trace, *.bak)
[/color][/b]
[b]What it is:[/b] Log and backup files created by mods or tools. Common examples:
[list]
[*][code]log.txt[/code]
[*][code]something.log[/code]
[*][code]trace.log[/code]
[*][code]*.bak[/code], [code]*.old[/code]
[/list][b]
Why it’s flagged:[/b] These files can grow over time and create clutter, especially if a mod writes logs every session.

[b]Is it safe to remove?
[/b]
Often yes, but:
[list]
[*]Logs can be useful when diagnosing crashes or reporting issues.
[*]Some mods intentionally ship a log/readme-like file (rare, but possible).
[/list][b]Why it’s caution:[/b] Removing them won’t usually break anything, but you might delete information you wanted for troubleshooting.
[line][b][color=#ffff00]CAUTION: Dev/build folders (bin/, obj/, .vs/, .git/, pycache/ etc.)
[/color][/b]
[b]What it is:[/b] Folders used for development, builds, or source control, such as:
[list]
[*][code]bin/[/code], [code]obj/[/code] (compiled build output)
[*][code].vs/[/code] (Visual Studio settings)
[*][code].git/[/code] (Git repository)
[*][code]__pycache__/[/code] (Python cache)
[*][code]node_modules/[/code] (JavaScript dependencies)
[/list][b]
Why it’s flagged:[/b] These folders are not needed for normal gameplay and can take up space or clutter the Mods directory.

[b]Is it safe to remove?
[/b]
For players: usually safe.

For mod authors: not always safe, because it may remove:

[list]
[*]source control history ([code].git[/code])
[*]project settings ([code].vs[/code])
[*]local build outputs you still want
[/list][b]Why it’s caution:[/b] It can delete important development files if the user is a mod author or keeps source projects inside Mods.

[b][color=#ffff00]Multiple manifest.json inside one top-level mod folder (Caution)
[/color][/b]
This tool can flag a top-level mod folder when it contains [b]more than one [code]manifest.json[/code][/b] somewhere inside it.

[b]Why this happens[/b]
[list]
[*]You extracted a mod update [b]on top of an existing folder[/b], leaving an old version inside.
[*]A ZIP was extracted with an extra wrapper folder, creating [b]nested copies[/b].
[*]An old backup/version folder was kept inside the mod directory.
[/list][b]Why it matters[/b]
[list]
[*]It usually indicates [b]leftover versions[/b] or [b]nested installs[/b], which can confuse manual troubleshooting.
[*]In some cases it can lead to duplicate/incorrect loading depending on how the folders are arranged.
[/list][b]Safety[/b]
[list]
[*]This is marked as [b]CAUTION[/b] and is [b]not auto-selected[/b].
[*]Some mod authors intentionally bundle multiple manifests (less common), so you should review the listed manifest paths before removing anything.
[/list][b]What the tool shows[/b]
[list]
[*]The top-level folder being flagged
[*]A list of [b]every [code]manifest.json[/code] path[/b] found inside, so you can quickly spot the extra copy and decide what to keep.
[/list]
